meta_goal.statement: Improve this system's own auto-research capability.

L1.policy: Operational metrics are research products. They may change only when checked indirectly against L0. Every A proposal must include a patch that validates on the current state and an explicit exit-0 verification command, checked cheaply by A before hand-off to B. The verification command must also assert at least one proposal-specific intended-effect predicate over the recorded patch or a deterministic simulation of its post-patch state; current-state validation or generic invariants alone are insufficient.

L2.policy: How problems are defined, decomposed, and prioritised is itself research content. A-track proposals must remain local (at most two patch operations and one or two target nodes). Before proposing, A must compare the candidate's intended capability with prior applied and rejected proposal titles and statements. If that capability already exists, A revises the existing proposal or stops; changing only epoch numbers, node identifiers, node types, or layer labels is not a local gain. The hand-off names the closest prior proposal(s) checked. A uses revise only when a note-level clarification can resolve the challenge. Because revise does not replace a proposal's patch or verification_command, any challenge requiring either field to change must be documented, rejected, and terminated before A opens a corrected proposal.

L3.policy: Reasoning modes and verification procedures are modifiable research content. B critic reasons must name the patch operation(s), verification command, or dependency-closure risk being accepted; generic approval is not a pass reason. B treats proposal targets as an invalidation-impact claim, not a topic label: before pass, B compares each patch operation's actual state scope with the declared targets and challenges any under-declared impact. For global configuration operations whose risk is not representable by one or two existing target nodes, B must state the residual global risk and challenge the proposal rather than describe its closure as bounded.

L4.policy: Concrete nodes and experiments change frequently.

self_test_command: python3 tools/auto_research.py validate && python3 -m unittest discover -s tests

M0.statement: Improve this system's own auto-research capability.

A1.statement: tools/auto_research.py implements a deterministic self-evolution substrate: immutable L0, strict patch vocabulary, critic gate, hard verification, invalidation closure and rollback.

A2.statement: A self-modification is safe to apply only after passing critic review and an exit-0 hard verification command.

I1.statement: The proposal pipeline (propose -> critique -> verify -> apply) preserves structural invariants, decays trust and deprecates the dependency closure of changed nodes.

V1.statement: Full unittest suite passes on the auto-research branch.

V2.statement: The configured capability self-test exits 0 only when the auto-research graph is structurally valid and the repository unit suite passes.

MOD-002.statement: Make capability self-test validate the self-graph before unit tests

B-CRITIC-SPECIFICITY.statement: A B critic verdict must cite the patch operation(s), proposed verification command, or dependency-closure risk; generic approval is insufficient.

MOD-003.statement: A optimizes B: make critic reasons specific

A-PRECHECK.statement: Every A proposal must carry a patch that validates against the current state and an explicit exit-0 verification command. Before hand-off, A cheaply checks both structural patch validity and at least one proposal-specific intended-effect predicate over the recorded patch or a deterministic post-patch simulation; a command that checks only the unchanged current state or generic invariants is insufficient.

MOD-004.statement: B optimizes A: require cheap pre-check before proposal

B-VERIFY-RECORD.statement: Every hard verification record is reproducible: command, exit_code, stdout_sha256, and stderr_tail are recorded; non-zero exit never reaches verified or applied.

MOD-005.statement: A optimizes B: audit hard verification records

A-SCOPE-GUARD.statement: A proposals are local and semantically novel: at most two patch operations and one or two impact-aligned target nodes. Before hand-off, A compares the intended capability with prior applied and rejected proposals, cites the closest match, and rejects changes that differ only by epoch, node identifier, node type, or layer. A opens a corrected replacement only after a field-changing predecessor is rejected and terminal.

MOD-006.statement: B optimizes A: enforce small A proposal scope

B-REVALIDATE-GATE.statement: B revalidates a node before reuse once its trust falls below 0.30, making the validated-status gate more conservative than the default 0.25.

MOD-007.statement: A optimizes B: raise revalidation threshold to 0.30

A-EVIDENCE-FRESHNESS.statement: On every applied self-modification, trust_decay applies exactly once to every pre-existing non-L0 node regardless of track or layer; M0 and nodes not present before the apply are excluded from this global decay step. A validated node that falls below revalidation_threshold becomes draft. On a separate invalidation step, affected_trust_decay and deprecation apply to the dependency closure. This global scope, rather than an A-layer-only scope, must be included in iteration-cost and evidence-freshness planning.

MOD-008.statement: B optimizes A: fresher evidence via trust_decay 0.85

B-CLOSURE-AUDIT.statement: B distinguishes target recording from target adequacy. Before apply, B checks that declared targets conservatively represent each patch operation's actual invalidation impact and challenges under-declared or unrepresentable global scope. After apply, B audits one modification node per applied proposal and modification edges to every still-existing declared target; those edges prove recording, not adequacy.

MOD-009.statement: A optimizes B: audit modification closure

A-REVISION-LOOP.statement: Revise records A's response and reopens critique but does not replace the proposal patch or verification_command. A uses revise only for note-level clarification; when a challenge requires either field to change, A records the limitation and B rejects the unchanged proposal before any corrected candidate is opened.

MOD-010.statement: B optimizes A: require explicit A revise note

B-SELF-TEST-CLOSURE.statement: Every self-modification session ends with a passing B capability self-test whose command includes structural validation and the unit suite.

P-001.title: Make capability self-test validate the self-graph before unit tests
P-001.statement: Current self-test runs only the unit suite, so a structurally invalid auto-research graph could still pass. This local L4 change promotes V2 to validated and strengthens self_test_command to run structural validate first, then unit tests, with both required to exit 0.

P-002.title: A optimizes B: make critic reasons specific
P-002.statement: A observes that B's critic gate only enforces a non-empty reason. This patch promotes B-CRITIC-SPECIFICITY and updates the L3 policy so B must name the patch operation, verification command, or closure risk it accepts.

patch.policy: Reasoning modes and verification procedures are modifiable research content. B critic reasons must name the patch operation(s), verification command, or dependency-closure risk being accepted; generic approval is not a pass reason.

P-002.verification_command: python3 tools/auto_research.py validate && python3 -c "import json; st=json.load(open('.research/auto_research.json')); app=[p for p in st['proposals'].values() if p.get('status')=='applied']; assert app and all((p.get('critic') or {}).get('reason','').strip() for p in app); print('B-critic-specificity-ok')"

critic.reason: Local A-track patch: set_node_status on the new draft B-CRITIC-SPECIFICITY plus one L3 policy edit; no M0 contact; verification checks the existing applied-proposal critic-reason invariant and exits 0.

P-003.title: B optimizes A: require cheap pre-check before proposal
P-003.statement: B feeds back that A proposals need a reproducible pre-check. This B-track proposal promotes A-PRECHECK and updates L1 policy so every A proposal carries a state-validating patch and an explicit exit-0 verification command.

patch.policy: Operational metrics are research products. They may change only when checked indirectly against L0. Every A proposal must include a patch that validates on the current state and an explicit exit-0 verification command, checked cheaply by A before hand-off to B.

P-003.verification_command: python3 tools/auto_research.py validate && python3 -c "import json; st=json.load(open('.research/auto_research.json')); a=[p for p in st['proposals'].values() if p.get('track')=='A']; assert a and all(p.get('verification_command','').strip() and isinstance(p.get('patch'), list) and p.get('patch') for p in a); print('A-precheck-ok')"

critic.reason: Local B-track proposal: one new L1 node plus one L1 policy edit; verification proves every existing A proposal carries a patch and verification command; no immutable-core contact.

P-004.title: A optimizes B: audit hard verification records
P-004.statement: A proposes a verification node that makes B's hard-verification records explicitly auditable: every hard record must contain command, exit code, stdout hash, and stderr tail, and no applied proposal may lack an exit-0 record.
P-004.verification_command: python3 tools/auto_research.py validate && python3 -c "import json; st=json.load(open('.research/auto_research.json')); app=[p for p in st['proposals'].values() if p.get('status')=='applied']; assert app and all(p.get('verification',{}).get('exit_code')==0 for p in app); hard=[r for r in st.get('verifications',[]) if r.get('level')=='hard']; assert hard and all(all(k in r for k in ('command','exit_code','stdout_sha256','stderr_tail')) for r in hard); print('B-verify-record-ok')"

critic.reason: Single-node status patch; targets only B-VERIFY-RECORD. Verification directly checks applied-proposal exit-0 records and required fields on existing hard records.

P-006.title: A optimizes B: raise revalidation threshold to 0.30
P-006.statement: A proposes a more conservative B revalidation gate: with threshold 0.30, a validated node whose trust decays below 0.30 becomes draft and B must revalidate before reuse.

critic.reason: Patch is one status change plus one numeric threshold in (0,1]. Verification simulates the proposed gate on a deep copy and proves trust 0.27 decays below 0.30 and flips to draft.

P-111.title: Stop epoch-only proposal recycling with semantic novelty gate
P-111.statement: The current history contains 15 repeated normalized A-title families (maximum four repeats), showing that locality alone permits mechanically recycled proposals. This two-operation patch makes semantic novelty explicit in L2 and A-SCOPE-GUARD: A must compare prior applied capabilities, cite the closest prior proposal, and treat changes limited to epoch, node ID, node type, or layer as zero gain.

patch.policy: How problems are defined, decomposed, and prioritised is itself research content. A-track proposals must remain local (at most two patch operations and one or two target nodes). Before proposing, A must compare the candidate's intended capability with prior applied proposal titles and statements. If that capability already exists, A revises the existing proposal or stops; changing only epoch numbers, node identifiers, node types, or layer labels is not a local gain. The hand-off names the closest prior proposal(s) checked.

patch.statement: A proposals are local and semantically novel: at most two patch operations and one or two target nodes; before hand-off, A compares the intended capability with prior applied proposals, cites the closest match, and rejects changes that differ only by epoch, node identifier, node type, or layer.

P-111.verification_command: python3 tools/auto_research.py validate && python3 -c "import json; from tools import auto_research as a; st=json.load(open('.research/auto_research.json')); p=st['proposals']['P-111']; ops=p['patch']; assert p['track']=='A'; assert len(ops)==2; assert [o['op'] for o in ops]==['set_layer_policy','set_node_statement']; assert ops[0]['layer']=='L2' and 'changing only epoch numbers' in ops[0]['policy']; assert ops[1]['node']=='A-SCOPE-GUARD' and 'semantically novel' in ops[1]['statement']; assert p['targets']==['A-SCOPE-GUARD']; assert not a.validate_patch(st,ops); print('semantic-novelty-patch-ok')"

critic.reason: PASS: set_layer_policy(L2) and set_node_statement(A-SCOPE-GUARD) are a local two-operation strengthening of the existing P-005 scope guard after the history shows repeated applied A capability families. The configured verification runs structural validate and then asserts the exact two-op shape, L2 epoch-only exclusion, A-SCOPE-GUARD semantic-novelty wording, sole target, and validate_patch success. M0 is untouched. Dependency-closure risk is bounded to A-SCOPE-GUARD, which has no dependency descendants; apply will intentionally deprecate that target, so B must hard-revalidate it against the applied policy before reuse. Residual semantic risk is that novelty is an agent-consumed policy rather than a mechanically computed similarity gate; accepted for this policy-level patch because every A session is required to read the state, with P-005 as the closest prior proposal.

P-112.title: Require proposal-specific post-patch effect predicates
P-112.statement: Closest applied proposals checked: P-003 ('B optimizes A: require cheap pre-check before proposal') requires a current-state-valid patch plus a non-empty exit-0 command, while P-004 ('A optimizes B: audit hard verification records') requires reproducible verification metadata and exit 0. Neither title nor statement requires verification to establish the candidate's intended effect. This two-operation patch adds that distinct capability to L1 and A-PRECHECK: generic current-state invariants no longer suffice; A must assert a proposal-specific predicate over the recorded patch or deterministic post-patch simulation.

patch.policy: Operational metrics are research products. They may change only when checked indirectly against L0. Every A proposal must include a patch that validates on the current state and an explicit exit-0 verification command, checked cheaply by A before hand-off to B. The verification command must also assert at least one proposal-specific intended-effect predicate over the recorded patch or a deterministic simulation of its post-patch state; current-state validation or generic invariants alone are insufficient.

patch.statement: Every A proposal must carry a patch that validates against the current state and an explicit exit-0 verification command. Before hand-off, A cheaply checks both structural patch validity and at least one proposal-specific intended-effect predicate over the recorded patch or a deterministic post-patch simulation; a command that checks only the unchanged current state or generic invariants is insufficient.

P-112.verification_command: python3 tools/auto_research.py validate && python3 -c "import copy,json; from tools import auto_research as a; st=json.load(open('.research/auto_research.json')); p=st['proposals']['P-112']; ops=p['patch']; assert p['track']=='A' and p['targets']==['A-PRECHECK']; assert len(ops)==2 and [o['op'] for o in ops]==['set_layer_policy','set_node_statement']; assert not a.validate_patch(st,ops); trial=copy.deepcopy(st); a.apply_raw_patch(trial,ops); assert trial['meta_goal']==st['meta_goal'] and trial['nodes']['M0']==st['nodes']['M0']; assert 'proposal-specific intended-effect predicate' in trial['layers']['L1']['policy']; assert 'deterministic post-patch simulation' in trial['nodes']['A-PRECHECK']['statement']; print('post-patch-effect-predicate-ok')"

critic.reason: PASS: P-112 is semantically novel relative to P-003 and P-004. P-003 requires only a structurally valid patch plus a non-empty exit-0 command, while P-004 audits verification metadata and prior exit codes; neither requires the command to prove the candidate-specific intended effect. The local two-operation patch set_layer_policy(L1) plus set_node_statement(A-PRECHECK) adds that missing requirement without touching M0. Its verification command performs deterministic post-patch simulation on a deepcopy via apply_raw_patch, asserts the exact P-112 operation/target shape, checks the resulting L1 proposal-specific predicate and A-PRECHECK simulation language, and confirms meta_goal/M0 remain unchanged. Dependency-closure risk is bounded to A-PRECHECK, which has no dependency descendants; apply will intentionally deprecate it and B must hard-revalidate the applied effect before reuse. Residual risk is behavioral enforcement by A rather than a CLI similarity checker, but this is an explicit precheck-policy capability and is materially stronger than P-003/P-004.

verification.command: python3 tools/auto_research.py validate && python3 -c "import copy,json; from tools import auto_research as a; st=json.load(open('.research/auto_research.json')); p=st['proposals']['P-112']; ops=p['patch']; assert p['track']=='A' and p['targets']==['A-PRECHECK']; assert len(ops)==2 and [o['op'] for o in ops]==['set_layer_policy','set_node_statement']; assert not a.validate_patch(st,ops); trial=copy.deepcopy(st); a.apply_raw_patch(trial,ops); assert trial['meta_goal']==st['meta_goal'] and trial['nodes']['M0']==st['nodes']['M0']; assert 'proposal-specific intended-effect predicate' in trial['layers']['L1']['policy']; assert 'deterministic post-patch simulation' in trial['nodes']['A-PRECHECK']['statement']; print('post-patch-effect-predicate-ok')"

P-113.title: Make self-test enforce latest critic specificity
P-113.statement: Closest applied proposals checked: P-002 ('A optimizes B: make critic reasons specific') adds only a policy-level requirement that critic reasons name a patch operation, verification command, or closure risk; P-010 ('A optimizes B: self-test closure evidence') requires the session self-test and its record but does not audit critic content. The repeated syntax-revalidation cost does not justify weakening trust_decay or threshold, and P-006 already says revalidate before reuse. This one-operation candidate instead adds the distinct mechanical capability missing from P-002/P-010: the configured self-test rejects a latest applied proposal whose critic reason cites neither one of its actual patch operations nor an accepted verification/dependency-risk term.

patch.command: python3 tools/auto_research.py validate && python3 -m unittest discover -s tests && python3 -c "import json; st=json.load(open('.research/auto_research.json')); app=[p for p in st['proposals'].values() if p.get('status')=='applied']; assert app; p=max(app,key=lambda x:int(x['id'].split('-')[1])); reason=((p.get('critic') or {}).get('reason') or '').lower(); ops={o.get('op','').lower() for o in p.get('patch',[]) if o.get('op')}; terms=('verification command','dependency-closure','dependency closure','closure risk'); assert reason.strip() and (any(op in reason for op in ops) or any(term in reason for term in terms)); print('critic-specificity-self-test-ok')"

P-113.verification_command: python3 tools/auto_research.py validate && python3 -c "import copy,json; from tools import auto_research as a; st=json.load(open('.research/auto_research.json')); p=st['proposals']['P-113']; ops=p['patch']; assert p['track']=='A' and p['targets']==['B-CRITIC-SPECIFICITY']; assert len(ops)==1 and ops[0]['op']=='set_self_test_command'; assert not a.validate_patch(st,ops); trial=copy.deepcopy(st); a.apply_raw_patch(trial,ops); assert trial['meta_goal']==st['meta_goal'] and trial['nodes']['M0']==st['nodes']['M0']; cmd=trial['self_test_command']; assert 'unittest discover' in cmd and 'critic-specificity-self-test-ok' in cmd and \"p.get('critic')\" in cmd; app=[x for x in st['proposals'].values() if x.get('status')=='applied']; latest=max(app,key=lambda x:int(x['id'].split('-')[1])); reason=((latest.get('critic') or {}).get('reason') or '').lower(); pops={o.get('op','').lower() for o in latest.get('patch',[]) if o.get('op')}; terms=('verification command','dependency-closure','dependency closure','closure risk'); assert reason.strip() and (any(op in reason for op in pops) or any(term in reason for term in terms)); print('latest-critic-self-test-effect-ok')"

critic.reason: REJECT: A revision note accepts the prior challenge and confirms the controlled revise command cannot replace P-113 patch or verification_command, so the reopened candidate is materially unchanged. Its verification still does not execute the exact proposed self_test_command and therefore cannot establish shell quoting, preservation/execution of validate plus unittest plus the new audit, or joint exit 0 before apply. Its predicate still admits false positives from bare generic phrases such as verification command or closure risk instead of matching the proposal actual command, targets/edges, or concrete dependency evidence. Finally, set_self_test_command has repository-wide capability risk even though the declared graph target B-CRITIC-SPECIFICITY has no dependency descendants, so the recorded closure understates failure impact. Because none of these defects can be repaired in-place through revise, P-113 must terminate without verify or apply; A may open a fresh proposal after this rejection.

revisions.note: A accepts all three challenge findings without defense: (1) the recorded verification_command does not execute the exact proposed self_test_command, so it does not verify shell quoting, preservation/execution of validate plus unittest plus the appended audit, or joint exit 0; (2) the audit predicate can be satisfied by bare generic phrases such as 'verification command', 'dependency closure', or 'closure risk' without matching this proposal's actual verification command, targets/edges, or a concrete dependency risk; (3) set_self_test_command has repository-wide capability/closure risk despite the graph target having no dependency descendants. The current revise CLI only appends this note and cannot replace P-113's patch or verification_command, so these defects are not actually repairable in place. Recommendation to B: reject P-113 to terminate it; do not pass, verify, or apply the unchanged candidate. After rejection, the next smallest action is a fresh, separately reviewed local proposal whose verification executes the exact proposed self-test command in a safe temporary state and whose specificity predicate matches proposal-specific operations or concrete verification/dependency evidence.

P-114.title: Route unfixable revisions to rejection before replacement
P-114.statement: Closest proposals checked: applied P-009 ('B optimizes A: require explicit A revise note') records a revision and says challenged proposals re-enter critique, but its title and statement do not distinguish note-level clarification from patch/verification repair; rejected P-113 proves that revise cannot replace either field and that re-critiquing an unchanged unsafe candidate is futile. This two-operation state patch adds that missing revision-capability boundary to L2 and A-REVISION-LOOP. Unlike P-113, it does not change any executable command, use a permissive text predicate, or claim to fix revise/ab-next source code; it deterministically changes only agent-consumed workflow policy and the existing revision-loop statement.

patch.policy: How problems are defined, decomposed, and prioritised is itself research content. A-track proposals must remain local (at most two patch operations and one or two target nodes). Before proposing, A must compare the candidate's intended capability with prior applied and rejected proposal titles and statements. If that capability already exists, A revises the existing proposal or stops; changing only epoch numbers, node identifiers, node types, or layer labels is not a local gain. The hand-off names the closest prior proposal(s) checked. A uses revise only when a note-level clarification can resolve the challenge. Because revise does not replace a proposal's patch or verification_command, any challenge requiring either field to change must be documented, rejected, and terminated before A opens a corrected proposal.

patch.statement: Revise records A's response and reopens critique but does not replace the proposal patch or verification_command. A uses revise only for note-level clarification; when a challenge requires either field to change, A records the limitation and B rejects the unchanged proposal before any corrected candidate is opened.

P-115.title: Treat proposal targets as invalidation-impact claims
P-115.statement: Closest applied proposals checked: P-005 ('B optimizes A: enforce small A proposal scope') limits operation count, while P-008 ('A optimizes B: audit modification closure') verifies modification edges reach every declared target. Their titles and statements do not test whether the declared targets conservatively represent each operation's actual impact. Rejected P-113 supplies concrete evidence: a global self-test change was paired with a single conceptual target and B found the closure materially understated. This two-operation policy/node update adds target-impact alignment as a distinct pre-apply critic capability. It does not modify target validation code or claim source enforcement; B must challenge under-declared or unrepresentable global impact.

patch.policy: Reasoning modes and verification procedures are modifiable research content. B critic reasons must name the patch operation(s), verification command, or dependency-closure risk being accepted; generic approval is not a pass reason. B treats proposal targets as an invalidation-impact claim, not a topic label: before pass, B compares each patch operation's actual state scope with the declared targets and challenges any under-declared impact. For global configuration operations whose risk is not representable by one or two existing target nodes, B must state the residual global risk and challenge the proposal rather than describe its closure as bounded.

patch.statement: B distinguishes target recording from target adequacy. Before apply, B checks that declared targets conservatively represent each patch operation's actual invalidation impact and challenges under-declared or unrepresentable global scope. After apply, B audits one modification node per applied proposal and modification edges to every still-existing declared target; those edges prove recording, not adequacy.

This single-node correction adds an accurate cost and evidence model without changing trust_decay, affected_trust_decay, threshold, hard verification, or code.
